title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 9
paragraphs: With such words Gyges resisted, afraid that some evil might come of it, but the king answered, “Take heart, Gyges, and do not be afraid — not of me, as though I were saying this only to test you, and not of my wife, as though any harm might come to you from her. I will arrange it from the start so that she does not even realize she has been seen by you. I will place you in the room where we sleep, behind the open door. After I have gone in, my wife will come in to lie down. There is a chair near the entrance of the room, and on it she will lay her garments one by one as she takes them off, so you will be able to look at her at your leisure. Then when she goes from the chair to the bed and her back is turned to you, take care that she does not see you as you slip out through the door.”
